notes.0-3: 'Something struck him as he rounded the corner' reads as a physical hit or as a thought occurring to him

notes.0-2: 'He found a good pitch' (at a fair or game) can be a good throw or a good spot to sell from
notes.0-3: 'That pitch was too high' fits a thrown ball or a musical tone
notes.0-4: 'The pitch was too high' can also describe steepness (a high-pitched roof); weaker but defensible without context
notes.2-3: 'The busker found a perfect pitch' can be a good selling/performing spot or the right musical tone
notes.3-4: 'high pitch' / 'low pitch' is standard for both a tone and the steepness of a roof

notes.1-3: 'a bank of batteries/generators' can be read as a reserve store or as a row of objects
notes.1-4: 'The bank was running low' (food bank, blood bank vs. a lender short of funds) supports either store of supplies or financial firm
notes.2-4: 'We met down by the bank' is the classic river-edge vs. financial-institution ambiguity
